name: What exterior remodeling projects usually require permits in LA County?

mainEntity.name: Which exterior remodeling projects usually require permits in Los Angeles County and surrounding cities?
mainEntity.text: Which exterior remodeling projects usually require permits in Los Angeles County and surrounding cities?

acceptedAnswer.text: Many exterior remodeling projects require permits because they affect structure, drainage, access, fire safety, or utilities. Common permit-triggering projects include decks, attached patio covers, pergolas, fences above local height limits, retaining walls, pools and spas, exterior door or window changes, stucco replacement when the wall assembly is altered, electrical additions for lighting or outdoor kitchens, plumbing for sinks or gas lines, and grading or drainage changes. Even projects that seem simple can require review if they are tied to an existing structure or create new loads. Cosmetic items such as painting, planting, or minor finish updates are more likely to be exempt, but homeowners should not assume that hardscape, pavers, or low walls are automatically exempt if they affect runoff or slope stability. Because nearby cities may have different thresholds, the safest approach is to confirm the rule with the local building department before ordering materials or signing a contract.
acceptedAnswer.description: Permits are commonly required for patios, decks, fences over certain heights, pools, retaining walls, window or door changes, stucco replacement, exterior structural work, electrical or plumbing additions, and grading. Cosmetic work like painting or some minor hardscape may be exempt. The permit trigger depends on whether the work affects structure, utilities, drainage, or safety.
